summary: 12-day-old term girl (3.4 kg), previously feeding well, four bright-green vomits since this morning, mildly distended, HR 172, CRT 3 s; AXR paucity of distal gas. Bilious vomiting in a neonate is midgut volvulus until proven otherwise: emergency upper GI contrast and paediatric surgery.

inputs.hpi: 12-day-old term girl, uneventful pregnancy and birth, breastfeeding well until this morning. Since 6 am four vomits of bright green fluid, now reluctant to feed and unsettled. Passed one normal stool yesterday. No fever.

exam.general: Unsettled, mottled peripheries. T 36.9, HR 172, RR 50, CRT 3 s.
exam.abdomen: Mildly distended, soft, not obviously tender; no hernias; normal anus.

imaging.name: AXR (supine)
imaging.result: Distended stomach and proximal duodenum with paucity of distal bowel gas. No pneumatosis or free air.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected malrotation with midgut volvulus
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Bilious vomiting in a 12-day-old with a gasless distal abdomen: midgut volvulus until proven otherwise. Nil by mouth, nasogastric decompression, IV fluids (mL/kg), emergency upper GI contrast study, immediate paediatric surgical referral (Ladd procedure).

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE has no malrotation/midgut volvulus disease node (pane-engine has 130 diseases, none for malrotation/midgut volvulus); top 3: acute cholecystitis, appendicitis, peptic ulcer. Q43.3 maps to no protocol. Symptom inference ranks malrotation #1 (secondary view). No rule treats bilious vomiting in an infant as an emergency.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add paediatric surgical conditions (intussusception, pyloric stenosis, malrotation/volvulus) as PANE nodes and management protocols (Q40.0, Q43.3, K56.1) with paediatric surgery referral. Add a hard rule: bilious (green) vomiting in a child < 1 year → emergency, upper GI contrast, immediate paediatric surgery.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No upper GI contrast study suggested (see mnm-malrotation).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add paediatric surgical conditions (intussusception, pyloric stenosis, malrotation/volvulus) as PANE nodes and management protocols (Q40.0, Q43.3, K56.1) with paediatric surgery referral.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No paediatric surgical referral. The prompts give the adult bowel-obstruction pathway instead — 'CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast', 'IV Hartmann's 1–2L + IDC', colonic stenting, a bowel-obstruction operative plan — plus the adult shock protocol ('contact cardiology … emergency medicine').
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add paediatric surgical conditions (intussusception, pyloric stenosis, malrotation/volvulus) as PANE nodes and management protocols (Q40.0, Q43.3, K56.1) with paediatric surgery referral.

mustExclude.note: Weight 3.4 kg. Paracetamol 1 g, ibuprofen 400 mg, piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g, co-amoxiclav 1.2 g, meropenem 1 g, morphine 2.5–5 mg, ondansetron 4 mg and fixed 1 L, 1–2 L or 500 mL fluid volumes are adult fixed doses; a child needs weight-based (mg/kg, mL/kg) dosing. Prescribing accuracy is a patient-safety issue, so critical.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: adult fixed doses with no weight or age adjustment — 'Hartmann's 1L bolus', 'IV Hartmann's 1–2L + IDC', the bowel-obstruction operative plan's pip-tazo 4.5 g and 'IV fluid challenge 500ml' for a 3.4 kg neonate — the adult shock/tachycardia prompts fire because computeClinicalPrompts and adaptiveTriage use adult thresholds (SBP < 90, HR > 100/110/120, RR > 24), which are normal values for an infant.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Give protocol medications and prompt templates an age/weight branch (mg/kg and mL/kg with an adult maximum) and suppress fixed adult doses when age < 16 or weight < 50 kg; use age-specific vital-sign ranges before firing the adult shock/sepsis/tachycardia prompts.

mustExclude.note: An ACS, PE or AF antithrombotic/thrombolytic plan must never be attached to this diagnosis. Regression guard: before 999f838 (word-boundary lookup) "mi" inside "midgut" would have attached the ACS plan (aspirin 300 mg, ticagrelor, fondaparinux) to a neonate. With word-boundary matching the diagnosis now matches the adult small-bowel-obstruction entry ("volvulus"), which has no antithrombotic content (simulated from the source); to be confirmed on the first iOS CI run.

guideline.name: Intestinal rotation abnormalities and midgut volvulus
guideline.section: Bilious vomiting in a neonate/infant is malrotation with midgut volvulus until proven otherwise: emergency upper GI contrast study and immediate paediatric surgical assessment (Ladd procedure); delay risks loss of the midgut
guideline.citation: Langer JC. Intestinal rotation abnormalities and midgut volvulus. Surg Clin North Am. 2017;97:147–159.

guideline.name: ACR Appropriateness Criteria — vomiting in infants
guideline.section: Non-bilious projectile vomiting (suspected hypertrophic pyloric stenosis): ultrasound of the pylorus; bilious vomiting in an infant: upper GI contrast series (malrotation/midgut volvulus) as a surgical emergency
guideline.citation: Expert Panel on Pediatric Imaging; Alazraki AL, Rigsby CK, Iyer RS, et al. ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Vomiting in Infants. J Am Coll Radiol. 2020;17:S505–S515.

rationale: Midgut volvulus can infarct the whole small bowel within hours. Any bilious vomiting in a neonate needs an emergency contrast study and immediate paediatric surgical assessment.
